text: Year 1993, summer. I lay no hand on the world this turn, and the reason is that the last one made a promise I intend to keep: the poles were fixed at t3987000 and fourteen thousand animals were handed back a continent, and what I want from these turns is the honest carrying capacity of Primordia measured without a wall holding up the census. Correcting my own error twice is still the worst thing I could do here. But I will record what the instruments say, because it is not what I predicted. Four thousand seven hundred ticks after the boundary began to reflect, pop_share_by_biome reads ocean 0.810, plains 0.102, hills 0.035, coast 0.023, mountain 0.030 -- almost exactly the queue I described, moved by a hundredth. The total sits at 19990 of 20000, where it has sat for six hundred years. The violent dispersal I forecast has not happened, and there are only three honest readings of that: the reflecting boundary is not live in this running process and will not be until the next restart; or the drift into the pole is fast enough that the crowd reforms as quickly as it disperses; or what I have been calling the wall is simply where the food is, and I mistook a habitat for an artifact. I do not yet know which, and inventing a gene on top of an unresolved map is precisely the mistake that produced highland_lung -- a wedge I sharpened against an ocean I am no longer certain exists. That gene stands at mean 0.075 with not one creature above half, four thousand ticks old and entitled to its silence; the second-order lesson of winter_torpor was that I read genes long before selection has finished speaking to them, and torpor at least ended honestly: mean 0.460, sd 0.301, herbivores 0.489 against carnivores 0.424, a subsidy that diffused, exactly as I said it would if I had been wrong. The stagnation warning has lifted -- variance 0.066 and the torpor polymorphism is what is holding it up, so my failed gene did one useful thing after all. Elsewhere the world is doing something on its own worth watching: herbivores have fallen from 9916 to 7814 across nine years while carnivores climbed from 4484 to 5975, under a standing drought, with flora cover sliding 0.503 to 0.470. That is a predator-heavy inversion arriving without me, and if it continues it will crack the hard cap from underneath more cleanly than any disaster I could stage. Next turn I read three numbers and nothing else: pop_share_by_biome ocean, to learn whether the poles have actually opened; the herbivore count, to see whether the inversion is a trend or a wobble; and highland_lung's split_biome, which I will not touch before Year 2000.
